items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: I think it was Alma or Velma, one of those wives.

ctx.x: I think it was Alma or Velma, one of those wives. And this is the truth. She was stoned. I think it was the first time she ever had a drink in her life. And two hours later -- she went on home, you know, like after the dance, and two hours after that, she died, went home and died that night. And she wasn't -- I guess she was about 17, 18 years old. And it was really a big shock. And in later years -- well, they called it acute indigestion, but it must have been a heart attack or something, you know. But it really,

you know, it was upsetting, it upset everybody. In later years, after I came to New York with Basie, I asked -- I reminded Louie of it. I says, "Pops, you remember that night, the first time I met you in Tulsa? We sat out and talked about four or five --" I talked to him about four or five hours, Gary, just talking. And I says, "You remember that time?" He says, "Yeah, I told you you'd make it to New York."
